text:
VEDAVYĀSA AND SARASVATĪ PŪJĀ • ENGLISH / IAST
Translation of the supplied six-page booklet
1
Śrī Vedavyāsa and Sarasvatī Pūjā
English instructions, Roman IAST mantras, and English
meanings
Complete translation of the six-page booklet supplied by the user. Original page numbers appear
with each section so that you can compare the translation with the source.
Reading this translation
Action translates the Kannada or procedural instruction. IAST gives the Sanskrit in Roman script.
Meaning gives its English sense. The meanings are readable translations, not a word-by-word
grammatical edition.
The source has several apparent typographical errors and some compressed, grammatically
uneven passages. These are identified where they affect reading or meaning. Straightforward
word spacing and punctuation have been regularized. Suggested repairs are explicitly identified;
uncertain passages are not presented as established Sanskrit. Vedic pitch accents are not
supplied by this booklet and are not reconstructed here.
The booklet follows a Madhva understanding of worship: Hari is the indwelling Lord of the other
deities. Its statements about divine forms and the order of meditation are translated within that
framework.
IAST key: ā, ī, ū are long vowels; ṛ is a vocalic r; ś and ṣ are two Sanskrit “sh” sounds; ṭ, ḍ, ṇ are
retroflex sounds; ṃ marks anusvāra; ḥ marks visarga. Bīja syllables such as hāṃ, daṃ, rāṃ, klīṃ,
bhāṃ, vyāṃ, śrīṃ, hrīṃ and duṃ are sacred seed syllables and are transliterated rather than
assigned a literal English meaning.
1. Preparation and initial remembrance
Original page 1
Action: Gather turmeric, kumkum, flowers, consecrated unbroken rice (mantrākṣata), a
pañcapātra (ritual water vessel), an uddharaṇe (ritual spoon), and all the sacred books. Arrange
the books neatly in order.
Perform ācamana, the ritual sipping of water, and contemplate the divine names beginning with
Keśava. The booklet gives only a fragment of the name sequence:
IAST
govindāya namaḥ | viṣṇave namaḥ | … | śrīkṛṣṇāya namaḥ |
Meaning: Salutations to Govinda; salutations to Viṣṇu; … salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Source limit: The intervening names and the complete ācamana procedure are not printed in this booklet.

VEDAVYĀSA AND SARASVATĪ PŪJĀ • ENGLISH / IAST
Translation of the supplied six-page booklet
2
2. Resolve for invocation: āvāhana-saṅkalpa
Original page 1
Action: State the ritual resolve, inserting the applicable calendar details. The printed formula is
abbreviated:
IAST
praṇavasya … saṃvatsare, dakṣiṇāyaṇe, śaradṛtau, āśvīja-māse, mūlā-nakṣatre, ___ yoge, ___
karaṇe, ___ vāre, sarasvatī/vedavyāsāṃ āvāhayāmi |
Meaning: In the year …, during the southern course of the sun, in the autumn season, in the
month of Āśvīja (Āśvayuja), under Mūlā nakṣatra, with the yoga …, karaṇa … and weekday …, I
invoke Sarasvatī/Vedavyāsa.
Text note: The initial “praṇavasya …” is an incomplete opening, not a complete sentence. The final
“sarasvatī/vedavyāsāṃ” is the booklet’s shorthand and is grammatically irregular. The separate invocations
later in the booklet give sarasvatīm āvāhayāmi and vedavyāsam āvāhayāmi. Do not treat the ellipsis as a
reconstructed full saṅkalpa.
3. What to contemplate during invocation
Original page 1; attributed in the booklet to the teaching of Śrī Devendra Tīrtha
Action and understanding: The books placed for worship are not themselves Vedavyāsa or
Sarasvatī. Śrī Vedavyāsa is present in those sacred texts, accompanied by his consorts
Caturkaparda and Ambhṛṇī, whom the booklet identifies as direct forms of Lakṣmī. Brahmā, Vāyu,
Rudra and the other deities worship him.
Pray that Vedavyāsa grants knowledge, devotion and detachment, and an interest in studying the
works of Śrīmad Ācārya (Madhvācārya).
At invocation, remember Hayagrīva, the embodiment of knowledge; the ten avatāras of the
Supreme Lord; Durgā; Mukhyaprāṇa; Sarasvatī and Bhāratī; Śeṣa and Garuḍa with their consorts;
and Ācārya Madhva. Offer mantrākṣata while remembering them.
4. Arrangement and sequence of invocation
Original page 1
Action: Place the Vedas, commentaries (bhāṣyas), Sarvamūla works, śāstras and other sacred
books on a pedestal. Cover them with a silk cloth. Make the resolve:
IAST
śrī vedavyāsa-preraṇayā, pustakeṣu sannihita-sarasvatyātmaka-śrī-vyāsa-paraśurāma-pūjāṃ
kariṣye |
Meaning: Inspired by Śrī Vedavyāsa, I shall perform the worship of Śrī Vyāsa and Paraśurāma in
the form associated with Sarasvatī, present in these books.

VEDAVYĀSA AND SARASVATĪ PŪJĀ • ENGLISH / IAST
Translation of the supplied six-page booklet
3
Interpretive note: “Sarasvatyātmaka” is compressed ritual language. Read it together with the booklet’s
later description of the indwelling Lord; it does not state that the physical books are themselves the deities.
Invoke Sarasvatī. In the luminous forms of the invoked deities, meditate upon Mukhyaprāṇa;
within Mukhyaprāṇa, meditate upon Śrī Vedavyāsa. Invoke Hayagrīva, Dattātreya, Paraśurāma,
Mahidāsa and Aitareya with the mantras given below. Perform worship of the pedestal (pīṭha-pūjā)
as part of the invocation.
Source limit: Although Mahidāsa and Aitareya are mentioned here, no separate invocation verses for them
are printed in this booklet.
5. Invocation of Śrī Hayagrīva
Original page 1
IAST
vande turaṅgavadanaṃ śaśibimbasaṃsthaṃ
candrāvadātam amṛtātmakaraiḥ samantāt |
aṇḍāntaraṃ bahir api pratibhāsayantaṃ
śaṅkhākṣapustaka-subodhayutābjabāhum |
nasto mukhād api nirantaram udgirantaṃ
vidyā aśeṣata utābjabhaveśamukhyaiḥ |
saṃsevyamānam atibhaktibharābhinamraiḥ
lakṣmyāmṛtena satataṃ pariṣicyamānam |
oṃ hāṃ hayagrīvāya namaḥ |
oṃ hayagrīvam āvāhayāmi |
Meaning: I bow to the horse-faced Lord, seated in the lunar disc, pure and white like the moon.
His nectar-filled rays illuminate the universe within and without. His lotus-like hands bear a conch,
a rosary, a book and the gesture of clear understanding. From his nose and mouth he continually
pours forth all knowledge. Brahmā, Śiva and the other leading deities serve him, bowing deeply
with abundant devotion. Lakṣmī continually bathes him with nectar. Oṃ, hāṃ: salutations to
Hayagrīva. Oṃ: I invoke Hayagrīva.
Text note: The booklet reads amṛtātmakaraiḥ and abhinamraiḥ. A parallel Tantrasārasaṅgraha text reads
amitātmakaraiḥ (“with immeasurable rays”) and avanamraiḥ (“bowed down”). The booklet’s readings are
retained above.

VEDAVYĀSA AND SARASVATĪ PŪJĀ • ENGLISH / IAST
Translation of the supplied six-page booklet
4
6. Meditation on Śrī Kapila and Dattātreya
Original page 2
IAST
prodyaddivākara-samānatanuṃ sahasra-
sūryorudīdhitibhir āpta-samastalokam |
jñānābhayāṅkitakaraṃ kapilaṃ ca dattaṃ
dhyāyed ajādisamitiṃ pratibodhayantam |
oṃ kapilāya namaḥ | kapilam āvāhayāmi |
oṃ daṃ dattātreyāya namaḥ | dattātreyam āvāhayāmi |
Meaning: Meditate upon Kapila and Datta, whose forms resemble the rising sun, whose vast
radiance, like that of a thousand suns, reaches all worlds. Their hands display the gestures of
knowledge and fearlessness. They awaken understanding in the assembly headed by Brahmā.
Oṃ: salutations to Kapila; I invoke Kapila. Oṃ, daṃ: salutations to Dattātreya; I invoke
Dattātreya.
7. Invocation of Śrī Rāma
Original page 2
IAST - with two suggested textual repairs noted below
śyāmaṃ ravīndvamita-dīdhitikāntiyuktaṃ
jñānaṃ śaraṃ ca dadhataṃ priyayā sametam |
svātmasvarūpam amitaṃ hanumanmukheṣu
sandarśayantam ajitaṃ smaratorugīrbhiḥ |
oṃ rāṃ rāmāya namaḥ |
oṃ rāmam āvāhayāmi |
Meaning: Remember the dark-hued, unconquered Rāma with exalted words of praise. His
brilliance is immeasurable, like the light of the sun and moon. He displays the sign of knowledge
and holds an arrow, accompanied by his beloved. He reveals his limitless, true nature to Hanumān
and the other leading devotees. Oṃ, rāṃ: salutations to Rāma. Oṃ: I invoke Rāma.
Text note: The booklet prints ravīndramita and smaratorugobhīḥ, both difficult readings. The parallel
Tantrasārasaṅgraha verse supports ravīndvamita and smaratorugīrbhiḥ; these are the readings used
above. “Jñānaṃ” is understood contextually as the knowledge gesture.

VEDAVYĀSA AND SARASVATĪ PŪJĀ • ENGLISH / IAST
Translation of the supplied six-page booklet
5
8. Invocation of Śrī Kṛṣṇa
Original page 2
IAST
dhyāyed dhariṃ maṇinibhaṃ jagadekavandyaṃ
saundaryasāram ariśaṅkhavarābhayāni |
dorbhir dadhānam ajitaṃ sarasaṃ ca bhaiṣmī-
satyāsametaṃ nikhilapradam indireśam |
oṃ klīṃ kṛṣṇāya namaḥ |
oṃ śrī kṛṣṇam āvāhayāmi |
Meaning: Meditate upon Hari, radiant like a jewel, the one revered by the whole world and the
essence of beauty. His hands hold the discus and conch and show the gestures of granting
blessings and fearlessness. Unconquered and gracious, he is accompanied by Bhaiṣmī (Rukmiṇī,
daughter of Bhīṣmaka) and Satyā (Satyabhāmā). He grants all things and is the Lord of Indirā
(Lakṣmī). Oṃ, klīṃ: salutations to Kṛṣṇa. Oṃ: I invoke Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
9. Invocation of Paraśurāma
Original page 2
IAST
aṅgāravarṇam abhito 'ṇḍabahiḥ prabhābhiḥ
vyāptaṃ paraśvadhadhanurdharam ekavīram |
dhyāyed ajeśapuruhūtamukhyaiḥ stuvadbhiḥ
āvītam ātmapadavīṃ pratipādayantam |
oṃ bhāṃ bhārgavāya namaḥ |
oṃ bhārgavarāmam āvāhayāmi |
Meaning: Meditate upon the uniquely heroic Lord, glowing like burning embers, whose radiance
spreads beyond the cosmic sphere. He bears an axe and a bow. He is surrounded by Brahmā,
Śiva, Indra and the other leading deities praising him, and he teaches the way to his own divine
state. Oṃ, bhāṃ: salutations to Bhārgava, the descendant of Bhṛgu. Oṃ: I invoke Bhārgava
Rāma, Paraśurāma.

VEDAVYĀSA AND SARASVATĪ PŪJĀ • ENGLISH / IAST
Translation of the supplied six-page booklet
6
10. Meditation for invocation of Nṛsiṃha
Original page 2
IAST - minor repairs noted below
dhyāyen nṛsiṃham uruvṛttaravitrinetraṃ
jānuprasaktakarayugmam athāparābhyām |
cakraṃ daraṃ ca dadhataṃ priyayā sametaṃ
tigmāṃśukoṭyadhikatejasam agryaśaktim |
Meaning: Meditate upon Nṛsiṃha, whose three large, round eyes shine like suns. One pair of
hands rests upon his knees, while the other two hold the discus and conch. He is accompanied by
his beloved. His brilliance exceeds that of ten million suns, and his power is supreme.
Text note: The booklet’s athāparābhyaṃ has been regularized to athāparābhyām, and agraśaktiṃ to
agryaśaktim, following the parallel verse. Unlike the neighboring sections, the booklet gives no separate “oṃ
… āvāhayāmi” formula here.
11. Invocation of Vedavyāsa
Original pages 2-3
IAST
vijñānarociḥ-paripūritāntaḥ-
bāhyāṇḍakośaṃ haritopalābham |
tarkābhayetaṃ vidhiśarvapūrva-
gīrvāṇavijñānadam ānato 'smi |
Meaning: I bow to him whose radiance of knowledge fills the cosmic sphere inside and out;
whose appearance is like a green jewel; who displays the gestures of reasoning and fearlessness;
and who gives true knowledge to the deities headed by Brahmā and Śiva.
Action: Offer mantrākṣata.
Vedavyāsa Gāyatrī
IAST - first printed occurrence
oṃ pūrṇaprajñānāya vidmahe pūrṇānandāya dhīmahi |
tan no vyāsaḥ pracodayāt |
oṃ vyāṃ vedavyāsāya namaḥ |
vedavyāsam āvāhayāmi |
Meaning: Oṃ. May we know him who possesses complete knowledge. We meditate upon him
who is complete bliss. May that Vyāsa inspire and guide us. Oṃ, vyāṃ: salutations to Vedavyāsa. I
invoke Vedavyāsa.

VEDAVYĀSA AND SARASVATĪ PŪJĀ • ENGLISH / IAST
Translation of the supplied six-page booklet
7
Text note: The booklet prints pūrṇaprajñānāya in this first occurrence and pūrṇajñānāya in the following
repetition. Both are recorded rather than silently merged.
12. Repeated Gāyatrī and meditation on Śrī (Lakṣmī)
Original page 3
IAST - second printed occurrence
oṃ pūrṇajñānāya vidmahe pūrṇānandāya dhīmahi |
tan no vyāsaḥ pracodayāt |
oṃ vyāṃ vedavyāsāya namaḥ |
vedavyāsam āvāhayāmi |
Meaning: Oṃ. May we know him who is complete knowledge. We meditate upon him who is
complete bliss. May Vyāsa inspire and guide us. Oṃ, vyāṃ: salutations to Vedavyāsa. I invoke
Vedavyāsa.
IAST - invocation as printed, with spacing regularized
oṃ kauśeyapītavasanāṃ |
oṃ lakṣmai namaḥ | lakṣmīm āvāhayāmi |
oṃ śrīṃ | oṃ śriyam āvāhayāmi |
Meaning: Oṃ: [she who is] clothed in yellow silk. Oṃ: salutations to Lakṣmī; I invoke Lakṣmī. Oṃ,
śrīṃ: Oṃ, I invoke Śrī.
Text note: The opening phrase is a fragment, and lakṣmai namaḥ is irregular as printed. The grammatical
form for “salutations to Lakṣmī” is lakṣmyai namaḥ.
IAST - meditation verse
oṃ kauśeyapītavasanām aravindanetrāṃ
tāmbūlanīlakusumābhaya-sadvaretām |
śyāmāṅkakāntisahitāṃ paramāṅkasaṃsthāṃ
dhyāyed vidhīśanutapādayugāṃ janitrīm |
Meaning: Meditate upon the divine Mother, dressed in yellow silk, with lotus-like eyes. She holds
betel and a blue flower and displays the gestures of fearlessness and auspicious blessing. She is
seated in the lap of the Supreme Lord, associated with the beauty of his dark form. Brahmā and
Śiva praise her two feet.
Text note: The printed compound śyāmāṅkakāntisahitām is unusual. The English gives its likely contextual
sense; it is not offered as a certain grammatical resolution.

VEDAVYĀSA AND SARASVATĪ PŪJĀ • ENGLISH / IAST
Translation of the supplied six-page booklet
8
13. Extended invocation of the indwelling Lord and the
associated deities
Original pages 3-4
This is one long ritual address. The IAST below preserves its sequence, with clearer punctuation
and minimal grammatical regularization. Several names and compounds are unevenly printed.
The English therefore gives the intended ritual sense rather than claiming a literal, fully resolved
syntax.
IAST - invocation of the indwelling Vyāsa
etat sacchāstra-pustaka-lipirekhānta-tejomayarekhāntaḥ-
prāṇarekhāyāṃ sthitaṃ dharmanārāyaṇa-mahidāsa-kapila-
dattātreya-hayagrīva-nārasiṃha-rāma-kṛṣṇa-paraśurāma-
vyāsa-hari-prājña-puruṣātmaka-sarvadevābhimāni-
sarvavidyādraṣṭṛ-śrī-brahmāṇī-bhāratyantargataṃ
strīrūpaṃ vyāsaṃ saṃmukhīkaromi |
Meaning: Within the luminous lines of the writing in this sacred book, in the line associated with
Prāṇa, I bring into my presence Vyāsa in a feminine form, indwelling Śrī Brahmāṇī (Sarasvatī) and
Bhāratī, who are associated with the vision of all knowledge. The address associates the
indwelling Lord with the forms Dharmanārāyaṇa, Mahidāsa, Kapila, Dattātreya, Hayagrīva,
Nārasiṃha, Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, Paraśurāma, Vyāsa, Hari, Prājña and Puruṣa, and with lordship over all
the deities.
Text note: “Prāṇarekhā” and the nested “lipirekhā/tejomayarekhā” expressions refer to the booklet’s
visualization of presence within written sacred texts; their technical detail is not explained in the source. The
source prints bhāratyantargata without a clear final case ending; -antargatam is a grammatical
regularization above. “Strīrūpaṃ vyāsaṃ” (“Vyāsa in a feminine form”) is explicitly present in the source and
has not been removed.

VEDAVYĀSA AND SARASVATĪ PŪJĀ • ENGLISH / IAST
Translation of the supplied six-page booklet
9
IAST - associated divine forms, sages and teachers
tatsannidhāne śrī-bhū-durgāmbhṛṇīṃ, hrīṃ māyā-
jayā-kṛtī-śāntī-lakṣmī-jayantī-jānakī-
satyā-rukmiṇī, svayaṃ prītyākhya-vyāsa-bhāryātmikāṃ ramāṃ,
brahmaprāṇa-śrīmadhanumadbhīmamadhvān,
sarasvatībhāratyau, śeṣa-rudra-pārvatī-vināyakān,
bādariṃ, jaiminiṃ, sumantuṃ, vaiśaṃpāyanaṃ,
āśmarathyaṃ, pailaṃ, kāśakṛtsnaṃ, lomaśaṃ,
etān vyāsaśiṣyān |
guṅgūṃ, sinīvālīṃ, rākāṃ, sarasvatīṃ,
indrāṇīṃ, varuṇānīṃ ca etāḥ sūktadevatāḥ |
śrīmadānandatīrtha-jayatīrtha-vyāsatīrthādīn,
bhāṣya-ṭīkā-ṭippaṇī-kartṝn āvāhayāmi |
kṛpayā saṃmukhībhavantu bhavantaḥ |
Meaning: In that divine presence I invoke Ramā (Lakṣmī), described through the forms Śrī, Bhū,
Durgā, Ambhṛṇī, Māyā, Jayā, Kṛtī, Śāntī, Lakṣmī, Jayantī, Jānakī, Satyā and Rukmiṇī, and as Prīti,
the consort of Vyāsa. I invoke Brahmā and Prāṇa; Śrī Hanumān, Bhīma and Madhva; Sarasvatī and
Bhāratī; Śeṣa, Rudra, Pārvatī and Vināyaka.
I invoke these disciples of Vyāsa: Bādari, Jaimini, Sumantu, Vaiśaṃpāyana, Āśmarathya, Paila,
Kāśakṛtsna and Lomaśa. I invoke these deities of the hymns: Guṅgū, Sinīvālī, Rākā, Sarasvatī,
Indrāṇī and Varuṇānī. I invoke Śrīmad Ānandatīrtha, Jayatīrtha, Vyāsatīrtha and the other authors
of bhāṣyas, ṭīkās and explanatory notes. Revered ones, please graciously turn toward me and be
present.
Text note: The source’s list uses some nonstandard case endings, including jaiminīṃ and indrāṇīṃm; the
clear name forms are regularized above. The forms kṛtī and śāntī follow the printed long vowels. The source’s
compound linking Brahmā, Prāṇa and Hanumān-Bhīma-Madhva is interpreted according to its accompanying
Madhva instructions.
Action: Pray in this way and offer flowers held together in the hands (puṣpāñjali).
14. Establishing the presence: “gṛhā vai pratiṣṭhā” passage
Original page 4
The booklet labels this passage “gṛhā vai pratiṣṭhā-sūkta.” Its text is unevenly printed; the
following is a close transliteration rather than a verified reconstruction of a Vedic edition.
IAST - source reading
tatpratiṣṭhitatamayā vācā śaṃstavyaṃ,
tasmād yady api dūra iva paśūn labhate,
gṛhān evai nānā jigamiṣati,
gṛhā hi paśūnāṃ pratiṣṭhā pratiṣṭhā uttamā pratiṣṭhā |

VEDAVYĀSA AND SARASVATĪ PŪJĀ • ENGLISH / IAST
Translation of the supplied six-page booklet
10
Meaning - approximate: It is to be praised with speech that is most firmly established.
Therefore, even when one acquires cattle at a distance, one wishes to bring them home. The
home is the foundation of the cattle: a firm foundation, the highest foundation.
Text note: The words gṛhān evai nānā do not give a secure grammatical reading. “Wishes to bring them
home” expresses the likely sense of the surrounding passage, not a word-for-word certainty. The introductory
label means “Homes are indeed the foundation.”
15. Invocation of Durgā
Original page 4
IAST
oṃ kauśeyaraktavasanāṃ kamalatrinetrāṃ |
cakrābjatarjana-suśūlayutābjahastām |
udyacchatārkasadṛśīṃ paramāṅkasaṃsthāṃ |
dhyāyed vidhīśanutapādayugāṃ janitrīm |
oṃ duṃ durgāyai namaḥ | durgām āvāhayāmi |
Meaning: Meditate upon the Mother, clothed in red silk, with three lotus-like eyes. Her lotus-like
hands bear the discus, lotus and fine trident and display the admonishing gesture. She shines like
a hundred rising suns and is seated in the lap of the Supreme Lord. Brahmā and Śiva praise her
feet. Oṃ, duṃ: salutations to Durgā; I invoke Durgā.
16. Invocation of Prāṇa (Mukhyaprāṇa)
Original page 4
IAST
udyadraviprakara-sannibham acyutāṅke
svāsīnam asya nutinutyavacaḥpravṛttim |
dhyāyed gadābhayakaraṃ sukṛtāñjaliṃ taṃ |
prāṇaṃ yatheṣṭatanum unnatakarmaśaktim |
oṃ prāṇāya namaḥ | prāṇam āvāhayāmi |
Meaning: Meditate upon Prāṇa, radiant like a multitude of rising suns, seated in Acyuta’s lap and
devoted to speaking his praise. He bears the mace and the gesture of fearlessness and offers
reverent añjali. He can assume a form according to his will and possesses exalted power of action.
Oṃ: salutations to Prāṇa; I invoke Prāṇa.
Text note: The booklet’s nutinutyavacaḥpravṛttim is uncertain; the intended reference to praising Acyuta
is clear from the context. Its final formula prints prāṇām āvāhayāmi; the grammatical prāṇam is used above.
The verse’s multiple hand descriptions are retained without imposing a particular number of hands.

VEDAVYĀSA AND SARASVATĪ PŪJĀ • ENGLISH / IAST
Translation of the supplied six-page booklet
11
17. Meditation on Sarasvatī
Original page 4
IAST - grammatical repairs identified below
udyaddivākara-samūhanibhāṃ
svabhartur aṅkasthitām abhaya-sadvarabāhuyugmām |
mudrāṃ ca tattvadṛśaye varapustakaṃ ca |
doryugmakena dadhatīṃ smaratātmasaṃsthām |
oṃ sarasvatyai namaḥ | sarasvatīm āvāhayāmi |
Meaning: Remember Sarasvatī, radiant like a multitude of rising suns and seated upon her
husband’s lap. One pair of hands displays fearlessness and auspicious blessing; another bears a
gesture for perceiving truth and an excellent book. Contemplate her inwardly. Oṃ: salutations to
Sarasvatī; I invoke Sarasvatī.
Text note: The booklet has aṅkasthim and mābhaya; these have been joined and regularized as
aṅkasthitām abhaya. The source’s final ātmasaṃsthām (“present within oneself”) is retained. The parallel
Tantrasārasaṅgraha verse instead ends ātmavidyām (“knowledge of the self”).
18. Meditation on Bhāratī
Original page 4
IAST
bhāratīṃ sarvavedāḍhyāṃ bhartur aṅkasthitāṃ satīm |
dhyāyantīṃ satataṃ viṣṇuṃ dhyāyet sarvārthasiddhaye |
oṃ bhāratyai namaḥ | bhāratīm āvāhayāmi |

24. Dismissal: visarjana
Original page 6
Action: Perform dismissal during the early part of the day when Śravaṇa nakṣatra is present.
IAST
uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate devayantas tvemahe |
upa pra yantu marutaḥ sudānava
indra prāśūr bhavā sacā |
yathāsthānam udvāsayāmi |
Meaning: Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati; we who seek the divine call upon you. May the generous
Maruts come forward. O Indra, be swift and be with us. I respectfully dismiss the invoked presence
to its proper abode.
Text note: The Vedic verse is Ṛgveda 1.40.1. Devayantas tvemahe represents the joined words
devayantaḥ tvā īmahe (“we, desiring the divine, invoke you”). The booklet writes marutas sudānava; the
standard saṃhitā reading marutaḥ sudānava is used above. IAST here does not reproduce Vedic pitch
accents.
Action: Perform dismissal with this mantra, gently moving the book to mark the completion of the
invocation.
On the day of dismissal, recite the mantra beginning “yasya smṛtyā ca,” chant the three-name
mantra (nāmatraya-mantra), and dedicate the worship to Kṛṣṇa (Kṛṣṇārpaṇa).

25. Study during the worship period
Original page 6
Instruction: After invoking Sarasvatī and Vedavyāsa, do not use the consecrated books for new
study. The four-day period from Mūlā through Śravaṇa is an anadhyayana period, a pause in
beginning new lessons.
Do not study a new lesson during this period. You may reflect upon lessons already learned and
may perform pārāyaṇa, devotional or customary recitation.
